sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-7: Develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions forming new molecules that support growth and/or release energy as this matter moves through an organism

note.text: Every cell needs a steady supply of energy to stay alive and do its job.

steps.title: Mitochondrion
steps.instruction: Trace the mitochondrion in the middle.

note.text: Mitochondria are where most of the cell's energy is released from food.
The folds give lots of surface for the reactions.

steps.title: Sugar in
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of sugar coming in.

note.text: Sugar, called glucose, comes from digested food and is carried to the cell in the blood.

steps.title: Oxygen in
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of oxygen coming in.

note.text: Oxygen comes from the lungs, also carried in the blood.

steps.title: Carbon dioxide out
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of carbon dioxide leaving.

note.text: The sugar's atoms are rearranged into carbon dioxide and water. The carbon dioxide you breathe out comes from this.

steps.title: Water out
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of water leaving.

note.text: Water is made too. No atoms are lost: they're only rearranged into new molecules.

steps.title: Energy
steps.instruction: Draw the big arrow of energy released.

note.text: The energy stored in the sugar is released, mostly as ATP, the cell's energy carrier, and some as heat.

steps.title: Inputs and outputs
steps.instruction: Pick what each numbered arrow carries.

mistakes.Carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide leaves the cell. Oxygen comes in.

steps.title: Compare
steps.question: How is cellular respiration related to photosynthesis?

options.text: It runs the other way: photosynthesis makes sugar and oxygen, respiration uses them
options.feedback: Yes. Photosynthesis stores energy in sugar; respiration releases it. Their inputs and outputs swap.
Look at the arrows. Respiration's inputs are photosynthesis's outputs.
All living cells do respiration, including plant cells and yours.
It breaks sugar down. Photosynthesis makes sugar.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.question: When you run, why do you breathe faster?

options.text: Muscle cells need more energy, so they use more oxygen and make more carbon dioxide
options.feedback: Right. Faster breathing brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide from working muscle cells.
Breathing faster supplies oxygen for respiration in the muscles.
Muscles use oxygen. Respiration in muscle cells needs more of it.
Sugar comes from food in the blood. Breathing brings in oxygen.
